description: SIFTEC compat suite, offered only when SIFTEC is loaded. Uses SIFTEC's own test commands (op needed).

scenes.title: SIFTEC factory: the buildings_a row of work-package-5 buildings (built once, marked by bedrock at 1190 160 970)
setup: execute in minecraft:overworld run forceload add 1180 960 1290 1040
execute in minecraft:overworld unless block 1190 160 970 minecraft:bedrock run siftec worldtest buildings_a view 0
execute in minecraft:overworld run setblock 1190 160 970 minecraft:bedrock
scenes.requiresNote: Builds SIFTEC's buildings_a row with SIFTEC's test command (siftec worldtest), which lives in SIFTEC's CI-only selftest mod, not in its release.
scenes.ciNote: Package 8 (Andre's follow-up): a Create fluid tank full of lava floats in front of the camera, so Create's fluid renderer draws an animated block sprite (lava) outside terrain; CI fails on any late redraw.

scenes.title: The Sift (Mielon's The Sift dimension; its own clock and weather pinned too)
setup: execute in the_sift:the_sift run time set 6000
execute in the_sift:the_sift run weather clear
execute in the_sift:the_sift positioned 0.5 0 0.5 positioned over motion_blocking run tp @a ~ ~4 ~ 45 20
scenes.ciVanillaDrawGateReason: Its average follows the runner's frame rate: below 20 fps every frame lines up with a game tick and draws the tick's extra draws, above it some don't. Run 40180107484, full: Quicksilver 154.0 average / 154 median at 15.1 fps, vanilla's measure run 135.58 / 154 at 22.64 fps (Vulkan: 153.97 / 154 at 15.8 fps against 153.94 / 154 at 12.37 fps). Gated against vanilla on the median (Andre's rule, 2026-10-25).
scenes.ciNote: Mob spawning is off for this scene and the mobs already there are sent away before it settles, in vanilla's runs and Quicksilver's alike: Andre's decision (package 3, 2026-10-25), as the sprites over the canyon were somewhere else in every run; they turned out to be the Sift's note particles, which CI's pin mod holds off (SiftParticlesMixin). The next scene turns spawning back on.

scenes.title: Create's Ponder index screen (Create Fly's /ponder index), looking up at the sky and a stone block above the HUB platform (package 7)
scenes.requiresNote: Create's Ponder screens come with Create (Create Fly in SIFTEC's pack).
scenes.ciNote: Opened with Create's client command, typed in chat in every run (drive.py's ciChat). The index lists every item with a Ponder scene; the scenes themselves keep moving (belts, kinetics, the nixie scene's dancing parrot), so the index is the Ponder screen CI checks. It runs before the map scene, so SIFTEC's minimap and map markers are not on yet (after it, the Quicksilver and measure runs show the map scene's markers twice, as each bench sets the map up again: 578 pixels in run 40266027605, and the minimap's edge over the HUB platform showed tiles of chunks generated during the run: 425 pixels in run 40260847921). Spectator (the preamble's), looking up: sky behind the screen and one stone block above the camera, so Quicksilver has terrain to draw here too (CI requires it in every scene).

scenes.title: SIFTEC fullscreen map, centred on a pinned player
scenes.skip: MapMod is being finished (Andre, 2026-10-30): the map scene is out of the bench and CI until then; with it, its limits are re-collected
setup: execute in minecraft:overworld positioned 300.5 0 -199.5 positioned over motion_blocking run tp @a ~ ~ ~
execute in minecraft:overworld unless block 300 -63 -200 minecraft:emerald_block run siftec worldtest map setup

scenes.ciNote: Strict-gated since package 7: its area is pre-generated in the CI world (and so recorded by SIFTEC's map there), the player is put at a fixed spot (spreadplayers landed a block either way, and the markers sit relative to it), random ticks and mob griefing are off in the CI world. Before, vanilla runs differed by up to 22,532 strict pixels here. SIFTEC's map setup (unlock, radar sweep, two markers) runs once per world: an emerald block deep under the spot marks it done, so a Quicksilver or measure run's bench (which sets the scene up again) no longer adds the markers a second time; with one player name in every session the markers show on the compass in later scenes and sessions (factory_flat: 328 pixels in run 40436256016).
scenes.requiresNote: SIFTEC's map unlocks through progression; its test command (siftec worldtest map) opens it, and that lives in SIFTEC's CI-only selftest mod, not in its release.

scenes.ciMapModNote: MapMod is being finished (Andre, 2026-10-30): MapMod's minimap shows here, so the strict check leaves its screen area out (ciStrictMask) and draw calls are gated against vanilla in the same run only, not main's baselines (any MapMod build is taken).
scenes.title: SIFTEC Build Gun hologram (green where the building fits) in front of a water pool, high above the terrain (package 3)
setup: item replace entity @a weapon.mainhand with minecraft:air
item replace entity @a weapon.mainhand with siftec:build_gun
scenes.ciNote: The Build Gun hologram is drawn by Create's outliner (SIFTEC's BuildGunClient), not as terrain, so it stays on its own path; the gates check that it still looks exactly as with vanilla in front of Quicksilver's translucent water. CI presses Tab once after the setup (the Build Gun's next-tab key: picks the first Power building, the Power Pole Mk.1; the selection stays for the bench). On a laptop, press Tab once with the Build Gun in hand before the bench starts measuring. The pool's floor is sea lanterns: up there water freezes over at random where block light is low (ice in vanilla's own runs, run 40121527770), and light 14 at the surface stops it. The last setup step moves the camera three blocks, so vanilla sorts the water again from where the picture is taken. Not run on Vulkan: lavapipe segfaults (libvulkan_lvp.so) as soon as the outliner draws, in vanilla's run too (runs 40115084815 and 40119107821).
scenes.ciSkipReason: Mesa's lavapipe Vulkan driver segfaults drawing Create's outliner (the hologram), in vanilla's run too

scenes.title: Normal play with the HUD on: hotbar with items, the chat open with a few lines, SIFTEC's compass strip and minimap, on a platform in front of a wall (package 7)
setup: item replace entity @a hotbar.0 with minecraft:diamond_sword
item replace entity @a hotbar.1 with minecraft:iron_pickaxe
item replace entity @a hotbar.2 with minecraft:oak_log 32
item replace entity @a hotbar.3 with minecraft:torch 64
item replace entity @a hotbar.4 with minecraft:bread 12
item replace entity @a hotbar.5 with minecraft:water_bucket
item replace entity @a hotbar.6 with minecraft:redstone 7
item replace entity @a hotbar.7 with siftec:build_gun
item replace entity @a hotbar.8 with minecraft:map
tellraw @a {"text":"[CI] The HUD scene: hotbar, chat, compass and minimap","color":"gold"}
tellraw @a {"text":"Line two of the chat, plain white text"}
tellraw @a {"text":"Line five: a longer line of chat text to see the wrap and the background width","color":"gray"}
tellraw @a {"text":"Line seven, so six lines show whatever came before"}
tellraw @a {"text":"Line eight: end of the chat","color":"yellow"}
scenes.ciNote: The chat is open (its lines fade with time otherwise, and an open chat shows them in full); chatHeightFocused 0.25 in CI shows the last 6 lines, all this scene's, and CI's pin mod holds the input box's cursor on. The spot (400 -110, in the CI world's pre-generated, explored map area) keeps the map scene's markers off the minimap, and facing south keeps them off the compass: each Quicksilver and measure run sets the map up again in its bench, which doubles the markers (578 pixels in run 40266027605). A gray concrete platform high above the ground with a gray concrete wall 16 blocks in front (no sun, no mob in view; Quicksilver draws the terrain). Concrete is one flat colour: Vulkan sampled a stone-brick wall's texture differently from GL on most pixels (runs 40414693058 and 40426298065), which left the strict check blind under the compass and the chat. After the fills, the #chunks step makes drive.py reload all chunks (F3+A; the wall once had a hole, a section not rebuilt in time, in run 40450860976's measure-full run) and clear the chat. drive.py also clears the chat (F3+D) before the setup, so it holds only the setup's lines in every run (bench messages in Quicksilver and measure runs moved the chat's scrollbar: 48 pixels in run 40404251173). Runs after the hologram scene and before create_ct, which hides the GUI (F1) for the rest of the session.

scenes.title: Create connected textures: walls of andesite casing (with a corner), brass casing, copper casing with a stone block set in it, and framed glass, each beside a non-connecting block (stone, glass) (package 4)
scenes.requiresNote: Create's casings and framed glass: without Create the scene would show only stone, so it is skipped.
scenes.ciNote: The design doc's done-when names Create's connected textures: Create draws them through the Fabric Renderer API, so these blocks are tessellated by Quicksilver's renderer in Quicksilver's runs and by Indigo in the vanilla runs. CT blocks in view: create:andesite_casing (a 5x4 wall plus a 3-block return at its west end), create:brass_casing (a 5x4 wall and a 3x3 floor patch in front), create:copper_casing (a 5x4 wall with minecraft:stone set in at its centre left), create:framed_glass (a 5x4 wall); each wall ends against minecraft:stone or minecraft:glass, which do not connect. CI presses F1 after the setup (vanilla's hide-GUI key): SIFTEC's minimap shows whichever tiles it has scanned, which differs from run to run (vanilla against vanilla up to 167 strict pixels in run 40274749083), and a single wrong connected-texture border is smaller than that. It is the suite's last scene, so the hidden GUI reaches only its own bench.
